claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with: **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children do you have, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 15 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 15 years old and lives with you.

Let me ask you: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Since Alex is 15 years old and lives with you in the UK, that's a good start.

Now I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in any approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending school?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in school - he's doing his GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. So Alex is 15, lives with you in the UK, and is in approved education (doing his GCSEs).

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all, and he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Are there any special circumstances that apply to Alex?** For example:
- Is he currently in hospital or care?
- Is he living with someone else for any period?
- Are there any other unusual circumstances I should know about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He just lives here with me full-time, goes to school, and that's it really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 15 years old, which is under the age limit of 16
- He lives with you in the UK, satisfying the residency requirement
- You are responsible for him as he lives with you full-time
- He is in approved education (doing his GCSEs at school)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He is not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right
- There are no special circumstances that would affect eligibility

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. 

**Please note:** Even after Alex turns 16, you can normally continue to receive Child Benefit as long as he stays in approved education or training, up until he turns 20.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
